Uncertainty of the Electron Density from Stark Broadening

Source: R/uncertainty.R
electron_density_uncertainty.Rd

Computes the electron density from the Stark width of a line, as electron_density(), with its standard uncertainty and confidence interval, from the standard error of the width and the uncertainty of the Stark parameter of the line.

Usage

electron_density_uncertainty(
  width,
  width_se = 0,
  method = "stark",
  stark = NULL,
  wavelength = NULL,
  temperature = NULL,
  reference_width = NULL,
  reference_density = 1e+17,
  reference_rsd = 0,
  tolerance = 0.5,
  level = 0.95,
  species = NULL
)

Arguments

width

The measured Stark full width at half maximum, in nm (see Details). A vector is allowed.

width_se

The standard error of width, in nm: one value, or one per width. Default is 0.

method

"stark" (default) or "halpha".

stark

For method = "stark": a tibble returned by starkb_lines(). Alternatively, give reference_width.

wavelength

For method = "stark" with stark: the wavelength of the line, in nm.

temperature

For method = "stark" with stark: the plasma temperature, in K.

reference_width

For method = "stark": the electron-impact Stark width (nm) at reference_density, when stark is not given.

reference_density

The density of reference_width, in cm\(^{-3}\). Default is \(10^{17}\).

reference_rsd

The relative standard uncertainty of the reference width: of the Stark parameter of the line (method = "stark"), or of the width law of H\(\alpha\) (method = "halpha"). Default is 0.

tolerance

For method = "stark" with stark: the largest difference between wavelength and the tabulated wavelength, in nm (see stark_width()). Default is 0.5.

level

The confidence level of the interval. Default is 0.95.

species

For method = "stark" with stark: the species of the line, such as "Ca II", required when stark has several species (see stark_width()).

Value

A tibble with one row per width: the width and width_se, the electron_density (cm\(^{-3}\)), its standard uncertainty se, its relative standard uncertainty rsd, and the lower and upper bounds of the interval. Pass se to plasma_uncertainty() as electron_density_se.

Details

The electron density is proportional to \((w / w_{ref})^p\), where \(w\) is the measured width, \(w_{ref}\) the reference width of the line (its Stark parameter, or the width law of H\(\alpha\)), \(p = 1\) for method = "stark" and \(p = 1 / 0.67823\) for method = "halpha". With lognormal errors of \(w\) and \(w_{ref}\), the density is lognormal, with $$\sigma_{\ln N_e} = p \sqrt{\ln(1 + u_w^2) + \ln(1 + u_{ref}^2)}$$ where \(u_w\) and \(u_{ref}\) are the relative standard uncertainties of the width and of the reference width. The interval is \(N_e e^{\pm z \sigma_{\ln N_e}}\), and the relative standard uncertainty is \(\sqrt{e^{\sigma^2_{\ln N_e}} - 1}\).

The width of H\(\alpha\) grows less than linearly with the density, so its relative uncertainty is amplified about 1.5 times in the density. The standard error of the width is that of the fit of the line (the std.error of the width in peak_fit()), or that of replicate measurements. The uncertainty of the reference width depends on its source: give it with reference_rsd. The weak dependence of the Stark width on the temperature is not propagated.

See also

electron_density(), plasma_uncertainty(), peak_fit()

Examples

# H-alpha width of 0.50 +/- 0.02 nm, with a 10% uncertainty of the width law
electron_density_uncertainty(0.5, width_se = 0.02, method = "halpha", reference_rsd = 0.1)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 7
#>   width width_se electron_density      se   rsd   lower   upper
#>   <dbl>    <dbl>            <dbl>   <dbl> <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>
#> 1   0.5     0.02          3.14e16 5.00e15 0.159 2.30e16 4.28e16

# a line with a Stark width of 0.012 nm at 1e17 cm-3, known within 20%
electron_density_uncertainty(0.024, width_se = 0.002, reference_width = 0.012,
                             reference_rsd = 0.2)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 7
#>   width width_se electron_density      se   rsd   lower   upper
#>   <dbl>    <dbl>            <dbl>   <dbl> <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>
#> 1 0.024    0.002             2e17 4.35e16 0.217 1.31e17 3.05e17
